sources.entry: Tolgee - Developer & translator friendly web-based localization platform enabling users to translate directly in the app they develop. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Java

summary.one_liner: Tolgee is an open-source, web-based localization platform that lets developers and translators edit translations directly inside the running app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Tolgee as an open-source alternative to Crowdin, Phrase, and Lokalise. It offers in-context translation: holding ALT/Option and clicking an element opens a dialog to edit its string, and this also works on a deployed production app through the Tolgee Tools Chrome plugin with an API key. It includes machine translation via DeepL, Google Translate, AWS Translate, and Azure Translator, plus an AI translator that uses screenshots, key and project descriptions, and translation memory. Other features are translation memory suggestions, auto translation of new keys, an activity log, comments on translations, and translation history. The README also mentions an MCP server so AI coding assistants can manage keys and translations, and SDKs and a CLI for integration.
use_cases: translate a web app's strings in context
let non-developers translate a deployed app
automate machine translation of new strings
keep translations consistent with translation memory
how_to_run: Sign up at app.tolgee.io or access your self-hosted instance
Follow a guide in the integration section of your project
For MCP server setup, see DEVELOPMENT.md
notable: In-context translation via ALT/Option-click, including on production apps
Chrome plugin for translating deployed apps with an API key
AI translator that uses screenshots, descriptions, and translation memory
MCP server for AI coding assistants to manage translations
Integrates through SDKs rather than only syncing files
caveats: The README does not state self-hosting requirements or platform limits
Hosted app.tolgee.io is offered alongside self-hosting; paid tiers are not described in the README
Machine translation requires configuring external services (DeepL, Google, AWS, Azure)
